merger_name: EQT Fund Management S.à r.l. – McGill and Partners Group

targets.name: MCGILL AND PARTNERS AUSTRALIA PTY LTD

party_page.name: Mcgill And Partners Australia Pty Ltd

merger_description:
The acquirers, Matrix Acquisition Bidco Ltd (**BidCo**) and Matrix Acquisition TopCo Ltd (**TopCo**), are special purpose vehicles indirectly wholly owned by EQT X, a private investment fund solely controlled by EQT Fund Management S.à r.l. (**EFMS**). EFMS is the alternative investment fund manager of EQT X, which forms part of the EQT group of investment funds. EFMS is wholly owned by EQT AB (publ) (Sweden).

Pursuant to a Sale and Purchase Deed dated 4 September 2026, BidCo and TopCo propose to acquire the entire issued share capital and sole control of McGill and Partners Group Ltd (**McGill and Partners**) from Thunderbolt Cayman Limited, a vehicle affiliated with Warburg Pincus LLC (the **Acquisition**).

McGill and Partners are a boutique specialist reinsurance broker that acts as an intermediary between clients and reinsurance markets, assisting corporate and institutional clients in identifying, structuring and placing coverage for complex and specialist commercial risks. McGill and Partners are headquartered in the United Kingdom, with various subsidiaries and offices located in other jurisdictions including Ireland, the United States, Bermuda, Australia, Switzerland and Sweden.

In Australia, McGill and Partners primarily operates through its Australian subsidiary, McGill and Partners Australia Pty Limited. Its business activities are limited to the supply of non-life facultative reinsurance broking services. It does not itself underwrite or assume insurance risk.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application, the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition. There is no horizontal or vertical overlap in
Australia between the parties (or its connected entities) in the supply
of reinsurance intermediary or broking services in Australia.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
